props.title: Up Periscope
props.initialSlug: WWII spy risks all for daring Pacific submarine mission

sections.content: Up Periscope (1959) represents a key entry in the post-WWII naval warfare subgenre, starring James Garner as Lieutenant Kenneth Braden. The film follows the tradition of taut submarine thrillers like Run Silent, Run Deep (1958) and The Enemy Below (1957), focusing on covert underwater operations in the Pacific Theater. Director Gordon Douglas brings claustrophobic tension to the underwater sequences, while the film's attention to military protocol and procedure influenced later submarine classics like The Hunt for Red October (1990).

sections.content: The submarine film genre reached its peak during the Cold War era, with Up Periscope arriving at a crucial transition point between WWII stories and Cold War narratives. The film's focus on special operations missions presaged later films like Gray Lady Down (1978) and U-571 (2000), while maintaining the documentary-like attention to detail that characterized 1950s war films. James Garner's performance established a template for submarine commanders that influenced characters in films like Crimson Tide (1995).

The technical achievements of Up Periscope deserve special attention, particularly its underwater photography by Carl E. Guthrie. These sequences built upon innovations from Operation Pacific (1951) and helped establish visual conventions that would become standard in submarine films like The Bedford Incident (1965) and Ice Station Zebra (1968). sections.content: The legacy of Up Periscope can be traced through later submarine thrillers like K-19: The Widowmaker (2002) and Hunter Killer (2018). The film's combination of special operations and underwater warfare particularly influenced Navy SEALs (1990) and Act of Valor (2012), showing how submarine warfare evolved to incorporate special forces operations.
